text:
sam: noticing a p99 CPU spike on telemetry-exporter around 11:15 during the new routing policy rollout. correlated with span volume increase from route B :thinking_face:
maya: saw that too, p50 fine, p99 went from 220ms -> 1.9s and CPU on exporter pods jumped 3x
li: do we have the exporter batching metrics? could be batch window collapse under high concurrency
telemetry-bot: export_queue_size: 72 -> 640 in 3m, exporter_threads: 8/8 saturated
felix: logs show a lot more fanout spans for user-features route (policy v2). each incoming trace spawns ~12 spans now vs 3 before
nora: that explains volume. Did we change sampling for that route?
sam: yes, config bumped to keep=100% for rollout testing. we forgot to increase exporter capacity or sampling fallback
maya: quick thought: either reduce keep to 10% for that route, or increase batching window and exporter threads temporarily
li: reducing keep is fastest mitigation. hajira (PM) wanted full fidelity for rollout metrics though
felix: can we do adaptive sampling: keep 100% for trace root + 5% for noisy routes?
sam: I can push a conservative sampler change now, reduce route B keep->15% and enable adaptive fallback
deploy-bot: sam triggered config change: /deploy configs/telemetry/samplers/route-B-15pct -- started
telemetry-bot: config applied on 6/6 collector instances, propagation ~ 20s
maya: while that rolls out, we should also tune exporter settings so p99 doesn't blow up if traffic spikes again
li: current exporter config in staging: 
```
exporter:
  threads: 8
  send_batch_size: 512
  send_batch_timeout_ms: 50
  queue_limit: 8192
```
li: on load the batch timeout is being starved because queue fills and threads block on network
felix: propose increasing threads to 12 and send_batch_timeout to 100ms. also enable backpressure metrics per-route
nora: downside is more threads -> more CPU. but if we combine with sampling it might be net lower CPU overall
sam: agreed. plan: immediate sampling reduction + rollout of exporter tuner: threads 12, timeout 100ms, queue_limit 12k as a cautious bump
maya: also add a temporary route-level shed rule: if exporter_queue_size > 6k then drop non-root spans from route B. keep roots only
li: config snippet for shed rule: 
```
route_policy:
  route_B:
    span_shed_threshold: 6000
    shed_keep: ["trace.root"]
```
li: I'll open a canary with 2 instances with new exporter settings first
telemetry-bot: canary started (2/2) with exporter_threads=12, timeout=100ms
telemetry-bot: metrics post-canary (1m): exporter_cpu -3%, p99 latency -30% on canary vs baseline
sam: nice. after canary we rolled to 50% and p99 dropped back to ~300ms
maya: logging shows per-request span fanout is the real culprit. for medium-term: we need a UX change in rollout console to surface span amplification risk when flipping routing policies (a warning and automatic suggested sampler)
felix: +1 on console hint. also add a telemetry knob: estimated added spans and estimated token CPU cost before applying policy
nora: ops checklist: 1) keep route-B sample at 15% 2) deploy exporter tuner to 100% 3) enable shed rule 4) add dashboard panel for per-route exporter queue and fanout ratio
sam: doing 1-3 now. creating dashboard patch after lunch
maya: follow-up: we should add an automatic policy that if exporter_queue_size growth rate > X for 30s, system auto-applies shed rule and notifies #eng-oncall
li: create a small alert playbook and an incident runbook entry, I'll draft it
telemetry-bot: alert rule created: export_queue_ingress_rate > 2000/s for 30s -> page oncall
sam: thanks. will monitor next 2h. if anyone sees anything odd ping me. :eyes:
